_meta.note: First domain adapter: heartbeat-code dep-lint (Seam 1 — plan authoring). It validates a dag.json's `requires` edges against a code dependency graph, so HeartBeat plans for CODE get correct sparse deps (the hardest authoring problem) without coupling code-awareness into the general method. BOUNDARY (the whole point): lives in plugin/adapters/code/, delivered by the plugin but NOT scaffolded into any .hb/, NOT core, NOT a parity surface (single-runtime node, like viz/bench/mcp-serve). Core (tick/state/resolver/lint/audit/gate) is untouched; the suites stay green without CodeGraph installed. The adapter consumes a narrow CONTRACT (codemap.json: symbol->symbol edges + task->symbols), so the value-bearing logic is proven hermetically against fixtures; CodeGraph is the first PROVIDER of that contract, and its live SQLite read is honestly harness-first (can't gate without CodeGraph). Spec-first throughout; adversarial review on both gates.

tasks.title: Author the dep-lint proof + fixtures (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/code-deplint.sh — a deterministic, self-contained proof that MUST fail before the engine exists (it invokes plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js, which is absent). Derive repo root from the script path; use `set -euo pipefail` with explicit per-assertion failure exits so a skipped/errored check cannot yield the marker. Author fixtures under plugin/adapters/code/fixtures/: (a) missing.dag.json + missing.codemap.json — tasks TA,TB with empty `requires`; edges [["symA","symB"]], tasks {TA:[symA],TB:[symB]} so symA depends on symB => TA should require TB (likely-MISSING). (b) redundant.dag.json + redundant.codemap.json — TA requires TB but NO symbol edge across their sets (over-constraint). (c) collision.dag.json + collision.codemap.json — TA,TB unordered (neither requires the other) but share a symbol symX (parallel-collision). (d) clean.dag.json + clean.codemap.json — `requires` exactly matches the edges, no overlap => zero findings. (e) transitive.dag.json + transitive.codemap.json — TA requires TB, TB requires TC (a chain); edge [["symA","symC"]] with tasks {TA:[symA],TC:[symC]} so TA depends on TC but is ALREADY ordered-after TC transitively => missing MUST be 0 (this fixture refutes a naive engine that only checks DIRECT requires). The proof asserts the EXACT outcome per fixture: missing.* => missing>=1 AND the suggested-edge detail line NAMES TA and TB (not just a count); redundant.* => redundant>=1; collision.* => collision>=1; clean.* => missing=0 redundant=0 collision=0; transitive.* => missing=0. AND strict semantics: `--strict` exits non-zero on missing.* and collision.*, and exits 0 on clean.*, redundant.* (advisory even under strict) and transitive.*. AND a BOUNDARY sub-check: `HB_NO_GIT=1` bootstrap a throwaway project via plugin/bootstrap.sh and assert its `.hb/` contains NO 'adapters/code' (the adapter is not scaffolded). Print CODE-DEPLINT-OK only when ALL hold. Fast (<5s): tiny JSON + one no-git bootstrap, few node spawns.

tasks.title: Implement the codemap contract + deplint.js engine
tasks.description: Create plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js: a pure engine deplint(dag, codemap) -> {missing:[], redundant:[], collision:[]} plus a CLI `node deplint.js <dag.json> <codemap.json> [--strict]`. codemap = { edges: [[from,to],...] (from depends on to), tasks: { TASKID: [sym,...] } }. Algorithm: build the requires transitive-closure (A ordered-after B if A reaches B via requires). MISSING: for tasks TA!=TB, if some symX in tasks[TA] and symY in tasks[TB] with edge symX->symY, and TA is NOT already ordered-after TB (closure), emit {from:TA, to:TB, via:[symX,symY]} = suggest `TA requires TB` (skip if the ordering is already satisfied transitively — so a covered dependency is NOT flagged). REDUNDANT: for each direct edge TA requires TB in the dag, if there is NO symbol edge in either direction across tasks[TA] x tasks[TB], emit {from:TA,to:TB} (soft over-constraint). COLLISION: for unordered task pairs (neither ordered-after the other in the closure) whose symbol sets intersect (share a symbol; treat symbols as the file/symbol identity), emit {a:TA,b:TB,shared:[...]}. Print one machine-checkable line `HB-CODE-DEPLINT: missing=<n> redundant=<m> collision=<k>` plus human-readable detail lines. Exit 0 by default (ADVISORY — never rewrites the dag); with --strict exit 1 iff missing>0 OR collision>0 (redundant does NOT fail strict — non-code deps are legitimate). Also write plugin/adapters/code/README.md documenting the codemap contract shape, the three finding kinds, the advisory-by-default stance, and that the adapter is NOT scaffolded into .hb and imports nothing from core. Pure Node stdlib only (no deps).

tasks.title: Wire the proof into the suite (T87)
tasks.description: Add node-suite group T87 to tests/run-tests.sh (after T86) with check T87.1 running docs/howto/gate-examples/code-deplint.sh and asserting its CODE-DEPLINT-OK marker (guard on `command -v node`). Keep the whole node suite green (bash tests/run-tests.sh). Do NOT modify plugin/bootstrap.sh — the adapter must stay out of the .hb scaffold (boundary invariant, gated by GATE_C0).

tasks.title: Author the codegraph-map proof + schema fixtures (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/code-map.sh — a deterministic proof that MUST fail before codegraph-map.js exists. Author a fixture plugin/adapters/code/fixtures/codegraph-rows.json shaped like our BEST-EFFORT model of CodeGraph's schema (unverified against a live DB — CodeGraph is not vendored in this repo, so the exact column/type names are our documented assumption, not confirmed): nodes = [{id, qualified_name, file, kind}, ...] and edges = [{from_id, to_id, type}, ...] where `type` includes BOTH dependency-bearing kinds (calls, imports, inheritance) AND at least one non-dependency kind that must be filtered out. Also author the EXPECTED codemap edges JSON. The proof runs `node plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-map.js <rows.json>` and asserts the emitted codemap.edges (1) resolves from_id/to_id to qualified_name, (2) INCLUDES the dependency-bearing edges, and (3) EXCLUDES the non-dependency edge type. Assert the mapped edges equal the expected set (order-insensitive). set -euo pipefail + explicit exits. Print CODE-MAP-OK only when all hold. Fast (<5s).

tasks.title: Implement codegraph-map.js (rows -> codemap) + harness-first DB reader
tasks.description: Create plugin/adapters/code/codegraph-map.js: a pure function mapCodegraph({nodes, edges}) -> { edges: [[qnFrom, qnTo], ...] } that resolves node id -> qualified_name and keeps only dependency-bearing edge types (a documented allowlist: calls, imports, inheritance; drop the rest). CLI `node codegraph-map.js <rows.json>` prints the codemap JSON. Add a THIN, clearly-marked harness-first entry readCodegraphDb(dbPath) that opens a CodeGraph .codegraph/codegraph.db and SELECTs nodes/edges into the rows shape — documented as requiring CodeGraph/sqlite and NOT wired into the suite (it degrades cleanly with a clear message when no db/sqlite is present; it is honestly unproven in-repo). Also add a documented BEST-EFFORT task->symbol name-match helper resolveTaskSymbols(dag, nodes) that maps task titles/descriptions to qualified_names by deterministic substring/segment match — clearly labeled advisory/fuzzy. Pure Node stdlib for the mapping (the DB read may shell out to the sqlite3 CLI, guarded).

tasks.title: Method skill + gated how-to + record the boundary
tasks.description: Author plugin/skills/code-aware-planning/SKILL.md — the method: index a repo with CodeGraph, run codegraph-map to produce a codemap, run deplint against your dag.json at /heartbeat plan time, and treat findings as ADVISORY (validate/adjust `requires`, never auto-rewrite). Author docs/howto/plan-code-aware-dags.md — a gated how-to that explains the contract, the workflow, references BOTH proofs by name (gate-examples/code-deplint.sh and gate-examples/code-map.sh), and is honest that the live CodeGraph DB read is harness-first (unproven in this repo). Add it to docs/howto/howto-list.md (section B Onboarding or F Operations). Add code-map.sh to the node suite as T87.2 (asserting CODE-MAP-OK). Record in planning/parity-notes.md that the code adapter (deplint + codegraph-map) is node-only and intentionally NOT a parity surface (like viz/bench/mcp-serve). Keep the node suite, prose-check (T79), and the self-audit (T81 referenced-proof integrity) all green.

GATE_C0.desc: The dep-lint engine genuinely detects missing/redundant/collision from a codemap (with transitive-closure ordering so a covered dep is not flagged), is advisory by default and red-under-strict on missing/collision, is proven hermetically and wired into the suite, and the adapter stays out of the .hb scaffold.

review.prompt: Refute that C0 is done. Is the engine REAL graph reasoning or a trivial counter — does it use the requires transitive closure so an already-satisfied (transitively-ordered) dependency is NOT flagged as missing? Does --strict actually go RED on missing.* and collision.* AND GREEN on clean.* (and stay green on redundant.* by design)? Could code-deplint.sh print CODE-DEPLINT-OK if a sub-assertion was skipped/errored (set -euo pipefail? explicit exits?) — i.e. vacuous? Does the missing-edge assertion check the SUGGESTED edge names the right tasks, not just a nonzero count? Is the adapter truly out of core and out of the .hb scaffold (bootstrap.sh unchanged; no import of core)? Does the proof FAIL before deplint.js exists (spec-first)?

criteria.desc: the dep-lint proof passes end-to-end (missing/redundant/collision/clean + strict semantics)
--strict goes red on a missing-edge dag and green on a clean dag (real detection, both directions)
the proof is wired into the node suite (runs it + asserts its marker)
strict red on collision, green on redundant, and a transitively-satisfied dep is NOT flagged (missing=0) — refutes flag-everything AND flag-nothing engines
boundary: the engine imports nothing from the repo tree (no relative require; -aF = force-text + literal dot, so the check isn't voided by a binary-detected file)

GATE_C1.desc: The CodeGraph provider mapping turns CodeGraph's real nodes/edges schema into the codemap contract (resolving qualified_name, filtering to dependency-bearing edge types), proven hermetically against schema-shaped fixtures and wired into the suite; the method skill + a prose-clean, self-audit-tracked how-to document the workflow honestly (live DB read is harness-first); the node-only/not-parity boundary is recorded.

review.prompt: Refute that C1 is done. Does codegraph-map map CodeGraph's ACTUAL schema (nodes.qualified_name, edges.from_id/to_id/type) and does the fixture reflect it? Does it FILTER to dependency-bearing edge types (dropping a non-dependency type present in the fixture), or does it pass everything through? Does code-map.sh FAIL before codegraph-map.js exists and is CODE-MAP-OK non-vacuous (set -e, explicit exits, order-insensitive equality of the expected edge set)? Is the how-to HONEST that the live .codegraph/codegraph.db read is harness-first / unproven in-repo (no overclaim of a working live hookup), does it reference proofs that actually exist AND are wired (self-audit), and does it pass prose-check (only real hb subcommands, links resolve)? Is the node-only, not-a-parity-surface divergence actually recorded in parity-notes.md?

criteria.desc: the codegraph-map proof passes (rows -> codemap: qualified_name resolved, dependency-bearing edges kept, others filtered)
the new how-to passes prose-integrity (links resolve, only real hb commands, substantive)
the mapping proof is wired into the node suite
the boundary is actually documented in parity-notes (the adapter is named AND stated node-only / not a parity surface)
